register.title: Turn on sync

subtitles.credentials: An account is only needed to sync between devices. Just a username and password — no email, no phone.
subtitles.kit: The only way to get your data back if you forget your password.
subtitles.totp: Two-factor protection is required: even with your password, nobody gets in without your phone.
subtitles.done: Entries are encrypted on this device and reach the server only in encrypted form.

register.passwordHint: At least 12 characters. A phrase of 4–5 random words is best: easy to remember, hard to guess.
register.passwordNote: Your password encrypts the key to your data. We don’t store it and can’t reset it — only your Recovery Key can restore access.

recoveryKit.label: Recovery Key
recoveryKit.explain: The Recovery Key restores access if you forget your password or lose your 2FA phone: together with a second factor — right away, without one — after 48 hours. It unlocks your data — keep it as safe as your password, but separately: in a password manager or on paper.
recoveryKit.warning: Without your password and Recovery Key, nobody can recover your data — not even us: we don’t have the key to your entries.
recoveryKit.saved: I’ve saved my Recovery Key in a safe place
recoveryKit.tailHint: A quick check that you saved it: for a key ending …-AB12-CD, type 12CD.
recoveryKit.tailError: Doesn’t match the key — check the last characters
recoveryKit.savedRequired: Confirm that you saved the key

file.title: Recovery Key
instructions: The Recovery Key restores access to your data if you forget your password or lose your 2FA phone.
Forgot your password: open the “Recover access” page (/recover), enter your username, this key and a 2FA code, then set a new password.
Lost your phone: sign in with your password and, at the code step, choose “No access to my 2FA app” — the key replaces the code and you set up 2FA again.
Lost both your password and your phone: on /recover, choose “No access to my 2FA app”. Access opens after 48 hours; all that time your signed-in devices show a warning and can cancel the recovery.
Keep it separate from your password: in a password manager or printed in a safe place. Never share it.
Without your password and Recovery Key, nobody can recover your data — not even the impact log team.
If you issue a new key in Settings, this one stops working.

recoveryKit.tailRequired: Enter the last 4 characters of the key

totp.step2: Enter the 6-digit code the app shows.

subtitles.key: Enter your username and the Recovery Key you saved when signing up. Then confirm it’s you with a 2FA code — or, if you don’t have your phone, wait 48 hours.
subtitles.password: Access confirmed. Set a new password: the old one stops working, and all sessions and remembered computers are reset.
subtitles.totp: Password saved. Two-factor protection is required, and your old phone is gone — connect an authenticator app again.
subtitles.done: You’re signed in with the new password. One more step to make the account safe again.
subtitles.doneDelay: Your new password and new 2FA are active. One more step to make the account safe again.

recover.keyHint: Starts with ILRK1. Case, spaces and dashes don’t matter.
recover.expired: Recovery took too long — start over: enter your username and Recovery Key again.
recover.cancelled: Access not restored: the new password was not sent, entries on this device are untouched.

subtitles.code: The Recovery Key works. Now the second factor — 6 digits from your authenticator app.
subtitles.started: Done: in 48 hours, access opens without your password and 2FA.
subtitles.pending: The countdown is already running — no need to start it again.
subtitles.ready: The 48 hours are over and nobody cancelled the recovery.

recoverFactor.codeLocked: Too many wrong codes — code checks are temporarily blocked. Try again later.
recoverFactor.explain: Without your password and without 2FA, recovery becomes available in {hours} hours. All that time your signed-in devices will show a warning and can cancel it — this protects your account if your Recovery Key falls into the wrong hands.

steps.return: In {hours} hours, come back to this page with your username and Recovery Key.
steps.finish: Set a new password and set up 2FA again.

recoverFactor.phoneFound: If you find your phone sooner, just enter a code — no need to wait.
recoverFactor.comeBack: Come back here with your username and Recovery Key after that time. You’ll have {days} days to finish the recovery — after that, the countdown has to be started again.
recoverFactor.cancelElsewhere: Recovery can’t be cancelled from here — only from a device where you’re signed in: it shows a warning right now.
recoverFactor.phoneFoundAction: Found your phone? Enter a 2FA code
recoverFactor.readyText: The {hours}-hour countdown is over. You can continue without 2FA until {until}.
recoverFactor.notStarted: No delayed recovery found: it was cancelled from a signed-in device or has expired. You can start the countdown again.

subtitles.key: Your password is correct. The Recovery Key replaces the app code, then you set up 2FA again.
subtitles.enroll: The Recovery Key works. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app and enter the code to finish signing in.
subtitles.done: Your new 2FA is active, the old one is off, and your other devices were signed out.

recoveryLogin.cancelled: Sign-in cancelled, entries on this device are untouched. Your new 2FA is already active — use its code next time you sign in.

reissueKey.title: Issue a new Recovery Key
reissueKey.text: Recommended: the key you just used may have been left somewhere. A new key replaces the old one immediately.
reissueKey.done: The new Recovery Key is active, the old one no longer works.

kdfChange.title: Password protection settings have changed
kdfChange.text: The server sent different password protection settings for this account than the ones you signed in with on this device before:
kdfChange.weaker: the Argon2id settings are weaker (less memory or fewer passes) — guessing your password from intercepted data gets cheaper
kdfChange.hint: This is expected if you changed your password or recovered access on another device. If you didn't, do not continue: the server may have swapped the settings to make guessing your password easier.
